First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/ad089d39428498123469a2ac7895f7d04b8b3ff9dac18a1698462bfc7fabae99.png)

Notice that the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=2$ along the $x$-axis.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/975f68d06bb52e162ad792987899509f4090c03ec1b55af6335982a2951f6bbf.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=4-(x-1)^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=5.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{[\,5-(4-(x-1)^{2})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{(1+(x-1)^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(1+2(x-1)^{2}+(x-1)^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}((x-1)^{4}+2(x-1)^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi (\frac{1}{5}(x-1)^{5}+\frac{2}{3}(x-1)^{3}+x)\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi (\frac{1}{5}+\frac{2}{3}+2-(-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{3}+0)) \\  & =\pi (\frac{43}{15}+\frac{13}{15}) \\  & =\frac{56\pi }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
